subject.title: [Docs/Question]: Recommended pattern for telemetry-only message lifecycle capture

question: What boundary should OpenClaw docs recommend for telemetry-only lifecycle capture that stores raw Telegram/WhatsApp content locally: internal HOOK.md, typed plugin hooks, or an external ClawHub hook/plugin package?
rationale: The answer affects raw message privacy, plugin trust, and outbound lifecycle reliability claims; automation should not choose that docs/security contract while outbound hook parity remains partially tracked elsewhere.

options.title: Document trusted-local pattern
options.body: Recommend a trusted local internal hook or typed plugin depending on whether the operator needs side effects only or ordered policy hooks, with explicit raw-content opt-in and per-channel smoke-test caveats.

options.title: Defer until parity work lands
options.body: Keep this issue open until outbound lifecycle parity is resolved, then document a stronger cross-channel reliability contract.

options.title: Route as external package only
options.body: Treat CRM lifecycle capture as a ClawHub package concern and document only the existing low-level hook APIs in OpenClaw core docs.

recommendation.title: Document trusted-local pattern
recommendation.body: Recommend a trusted local internal hook or typed plugin depending on whether the operator needs side effects only or ordered policy hooks, with explicit raw-content opt-in and per-channel smoke-test caveats.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across hook contract decisions and the related message-hook boundary discussion.
